title: Numerical Investigation of Seismic Performance of RC Columns with Prestressed BFRP Jacket
content: According to the requirements of the current seismic design code, reinforced concrete (RC) piers of existing bridges generally have insufficient stirrup ratio, and need to be reinforced effectively. Tensioned fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) can provide active constraint to the core concrete, effectively avoid stress hysteresis of FRP, make full use of its high-strength mechanical property, and significantly improve the seismic resistance capacity of bridge piers. Basalt fiber reinforced polymer (BFRP) has high ultimate strain and the advantages of environmental protection, abundant raw materials and low cost, which leads it to be more suitable for seismic reinforcement than other types of FRP. In this paper, we innovatively propose the method to reinforce RC column by using hoop tensioned BFRP jacket, and the seismic performance is investigated by numerical simulation. The results show that this measure can significantly improve the ductility and energy dissipation capacity of the column, BFRP is even better than carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) to columns with normal strength concrete, degree of prestressing is optimized to be about 0.3, it takes best advantage when the column’s axial compression ratio is about 0.3, the reinforcement effect becomes better with the increase of the jacket height. This paper provides a new optional approach to the seismic reinforcement of existing concrete structures.
